🌍 Minister emphasizes importance of National Day of Fight Against Global Arrogance

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Minister of Education Alireza Kazemi says the ongoing circumstances in the face of the continued hostile enemy hostilities have increased the Iranian nation’s responsibilities during this year’s commemorations of the 1979 US Embassy takeover, known as the National Day of the Fight against Global Arrogance.

Speaking at a coordination meeting for the events, also remembered as National Student Day, Kazemi highlighted the historical significance of the occasion, calling the 13th day of the Persian calendar month of Aban, or November 4th, the peak of the Anti-Arrogance Week.
​
He pointed to several key events associated with the period, including the Student Basij Week, the anniversary of the martyrdom of Mohammad Hossein Fahmideh; the 1964 exile of Imam Khomeini; and the US Embassy seizure.
​
Stressing that the occasion must be utilized to strengthen the spirit against global arrogance, he said the US-Israeli war of aggression and consistent conspiracies by the enemies have doubled the significance of this week to show steadfastness and resistance through national unity and cohesion.
​
Kazemi also pointed to the global resonance of the Iranian nation’s resilience, emphasizing the necessity of upholding the legacy of the martyrs in order to turn the world’s attention to their steadfastness and to demonstrate their unshakeable resolve in defending Iran.
​
In the first quarter of November every year, Iranians, along with school and university students, hold large rallies across the country to express their discontent with US policies and to honor those who stormed the American Embassy — known in Iran as the Den of Espionage —capturing its personnel and documents that revealed Washington’s divisive plots.

@BRICSNewspaper

⚡️ Baqaei: Tehran meeting to focus on endogenous security

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei says that Tehran will host senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey later on Monday, with regional security topping the agenda of the talks. He says that the discussions could pave the way for measures to ensure security in West Asia through regional efforts.

Speaking at his weekly press briefing on Monday, Baqaei said the visit by the three countries’ officials followed a proposal by Pakistan during Army Chief Field Marshal Asim Munir’s visit to Tehran last week.
​
Saudi Defense Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman, Munir, and Turkey’s intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin are scheduled to hold talks with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council Mohsen Rezaie.
​
The meeting marks the first talks between Iran and the three Mecca Pact countries since they signed the agreement in August.
​
Baqaei said the talks would address key regional security issues, including Israel’s expansionism, developments in the occupied Palestinian territories, Lebanon, and the consequences of the US military aggression against Iran.
​
“Naturally, the meeting is expected to address the most important issues affecting regional security, including the Zionist regime’s expansionism, developments in the occupied Palestinian territories, and the areas surrounding Lebanon. Such a meeting cannot take place without considering the implications of the US military aggression against Iran for security across the region. This, too, is an important issue that should be addressed in this context,” he said.
​
He said the meeting could pave the way for further steps toward establishing a regional security framework based on the interests and priorities of regional countries.
​
“In our view, it is a positive development that regional countries are seeking to establish, or at least consider, regional security mechanisms based on their own interests and priorities. This meeting could pave the way for further steps toward establishing an indigenous security framework, a goal we have consistently advocated for decades, stressing that regional security can only be ensured by relying on the will and security considerations of the countries in the region themselves.”
​
Baqaei added that developments over the past two years, particularly the past eight months, had shown that lasting regional security depended on trust and cooperation among countries in the region.
​

📌 Tehran, IRNA — Indonesia supports Iran amid the ongoing war and calls for an end to hostilities, says Rolliansyah (Roy) Soemirat, Indonesian Ambassador to Iran.

💬 Araghchi urges cooperation to stabilize global gas markets

📌 Tehran, IRNA — Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has emphasized that constructive dialogue, responsible conduct and mutual fulfilment of commitments can ease tensions, ensure safe shipping and help stabilize global energy markets, arguing that the outcome depends on the United States’ political choices.

In an article published by the Moscow-based Vedomosti newspaper, Araghchi described energy security, alongside food security, as one of the biggest challenges, attributing the pressures to coercive US actions in the region.
​
According to estimates by the International Energy Agency, more than 112 billion cubic meters of liquefied natural gas (LNG) passed through the Strait of Hormuz in 2025, accounting for nearly one-fifth of global LNG trade, Araghchi wrote. He said the recent US–Israeli acts of aggression against Iran and continued military threats had led to the strait’s closure, disrupting gas supplies, particularly in Asia.
​
Gas prices in Europe have risen sharply, he said, while storage levels ahead of winter remain well below those recorded a year earlier. Similar pressures are being felt elsewhere, especially in Asia, which consumes 90 percent of the gas transiting the strait. Any disruption, he added, has consequences well beyond the region, affecting energy security, market stability and the economic interests of producers and consumers worldwide.
​
Araghchi called on producers to strengthen dialogue, diversify supply routes, protect critical infrastructure and develop practical mechanisms to limit the impact of geopolitical shocks. He said President Masoud Pezeshkian was due to discuss these issues in Moscow this week with counterparts from 11 gas-producing countries.
​
The Global Gas Outlook 2055, prepared by the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF), projects that 86 percent of global gas production by 2055 will come from fields that are not currently producing. Iran, which ranks second after Russia in proven natural gas reserves, is among the countries with potential, Araghchi said.
​
The outlook also projects that GECF members’ share of global gas production will rise from 38 percent in 2024 to 44 percent in 2055, accounting for 65 percent of net growth in global output.
​
Araghchi said energy cooperation between Iran and Russia could strengthen energy security, expand export capacity and encourage joint investment. Potential areas include Russian investment in Iranian oil and gas fields, technology transfer, equipment supplies and joint engineering.
​
He acknowledged obstacles, including US military action and unilateral coercive measures, substantial infrastructure investment requirements, and the complexity of long-term contracts.
​
Iran, he wrote, has proposed a seven-day plan to pave the way for reopening the Strait of Hormuz and restoring normal maritime traffic, provided conditions are met and military threats are removed.
​
Araghchi said market stability requires political will, mutual trust, cooperation, and peaceful settlement of disputes.
